p: We have need to walk in wisdom towards those that are without, to keep our mouth when the wicked is before us, and to be upon the reserve.

The discharge Achish gives him is very honourable, and not a final discharge, but only from the present service. He signifies the great pleasure and satisfaction he had taken in him and in his conversation: Thou art good in my sight as an angel of God, v. 9. Wise and good men will gain respect, wherever they go, from all that know how to make a right estimate of persons and things, though of different professions in religion.

God's people should behave themselves always so inoffensively as if possible to get the good word of all they have dealings with; and it is a debt we owe to those who have acquitted themselves well to give them the praise of it.

"The king loves thee entirely, and would venture his life in thy hand; but the lords favour thee not, and we must not disoblige them, nor can we oppose them; therefore return and go in peace." He had better part with his favourite than occasion a disgust among his generals and a mutiny in his army.
No one knows how strong the temptation is to compliment and dissemble which those are in that attend great men, and how hard it is to avoid it.
